Session chair's note – Ramesh, student research day
Irawati's project on monsoon crop yields is one of the strongest this year; I've seen her data. She told me before the session she hadn't rehearsed. 'I know it inside out,' she said.
Her slot was ten minutes. She spent the first four on how she got interested in farming, with photos of her grandfather's fields. The next five went on data cleaning, in detail. At nine minutes she was still on the method. I showed her the one-minute card. She said, 'Just one more thing,' and started a new story.
At ten minutes I had to stop her. The main result, that one change in sowing raised yields by a fifth, never appeared on screen. The judges marked her down for an incomplete talk.
Afterwards she looked stunned. I told her the work is excellent; the talk needs a timer.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel afterwards, and why?
qa.a: She looked stunned and was likely embarrassed, since strong work was marked down because she ran out of time before the main result.

qa.q: What could Irawati do before her next talk?
qa.a: Rehearse with a timer, put the main result early, and cut the background stories to a minute.

qa.q: How did the session look to Ramesh, the chair?
qa.a: Ramesh knew the work was excellent and was sorry to have to stop her before the result appeared.

grounding: Shows a student who knows the project well skipping rehearsal, running past the time limit and being cut off before the main result.

passage:
Friday
I'm so angry at myself. I knew this project better than anyone in the class, so I didn't rehearse. Why would I? It's my data. Disha asked twice if I wanted a practice run and I said, 'I'll be fine, I'll just talk.'
And I did just talk. I started with how we chose the site, then got into the problems with the sensors, then a funny story about the monkey that stole a cable. People laughed. I relaxed. I talked more.
Then Ma'am said, 'Time, Binita.' Twelve minutes gone. I hadn't even reached the results slide, the one with the graph showing the river got cleaner after the village drains were fixed. That graph was the whole point.
Disha had to give our conclusion in one sentence while I sat down.
Next time: timer. Rehearse. Results first. I owe Disha a samosa and an apology.

qa.q: What did the results graph show?
qa.a: The river got cleaner after the village drains were fixed.

qa.q: How does Binita feel about the presentation?
qa.a: Binita feels angry and ashamed, knowing the most important graph never got shown because rehearsal was skipped.

qa.q: What would you change first before Binita's next talk?
qa.a: Rehearse aloud with a timer and put the results early, so the key graph is shown even if time runs short.

qa.q: What was it like for Disha at the end?
qa.a: Disha had to squeeze their conclusion into one sentence on the spot, after offering a practice run twice.
